title: Follow-up: raise L40S KV cache headroom defaults to reduce OOM risk
author: Samir Qureshi
description: Context: We’ve seen intermittent OOMs on the L40S pool under bursty traffic + mixed prompt lengths (SUP-21958). The current L40S profile KV cache sizing leaves too little allocator headroom once fragmentation kicks in (especially after a few minutes of mixed prefill/decode and model reloads). This PR tightens the L40S safe defaults by increasing KV cache headroom and updating compaction/fragmentation guardrails + tests. Summary of changes: (1) L40S profile: reduce default KV cache target utilization and reserve more memory headroom for non-KV allocations (activations, workspace, CUDA graphs, allocator metadata). (2) Adjust compaction trigger thresholds so we compact earlier on L40S to prevent long-lived fragmentation from pushing us over the cliff during bursts. (3) Add a regression test that simulates a burst pattern and asserts we don’t exceed profile-enforced headroom limits; update golden profile snapshots accordingly. (4) Update logging: startup profile summary now emits the computed kv_cache_budget_bytes and headroom_bytes (only at INFO, no per-request logs). Knobs (effective): - L40S: kv_cache.target_gpu_mem_utilization: 0.86 -> 0.80 - L40S: kv_cache.min_headroom_mb: 1536 -> 2560 - L40S: allocator.fragmentation_soft_limit: 0.18 -> 0.14 - L40S: kv_cache.compaction.trigger_utilization: 0.92 -> 0.88 Notes / tradeoffs: - Throughput impact: expected small decrease on decode-heavy workloads that were previously saturating KV cache. Based on benchmark-lab spot runs (L40S, llama-3.1-8b-instruct, mixed bucket), tokens/sec -2.5% to -4.0% but p99 OOM rate goes to ~0 on the burst scenario we reproduced. - Tail latency: should improve slightly under burst due to fewer emergency compactions / allocator stalls; measured p99 improved ~3–7% in our burst test because we avoid retries. Rollout: This only affects L40S profiles in the profile pack. H100/B200 unaffected. Will ride with runtime-1.22 defaults; safe to backport to the 1.22 release branch if SRE wants it earlier for the L40S pool. Validation: - Unit tests: updated profile schema golden snapshots; new burst OOM regression test. - Perf: ran a small subset of benchmark matrix (short/med prompts, concurrency 8/16) on L40S; results attached in Linear ENG-4926 comment. - Manual: verified /health and debug endpoint report the same profile_id/profile_version and computed KV cache budget after these changes. Follow-ups: - If we see >5% throughput drop on L40S in production for certain customers, we should consider a separate “l40s_high_throughput” opt-in profile with explicit guardrails and SRE signoff (not part of this PR).
commits: runtime/profiles: adjust L40S kv_cache headroom + utilization defaults
runtime/memory: compact earlier on L40S when fragmentation estimate rises
tests: add burst OOM regression scenario for L40S profile
docs/comments: clarify L40S headroom rationale in profile pack examples
ci_checks: perf-canary (compare vs main): PASS (no p99 regression >2% on non-burst buckets)
review_conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): Can you clarify whether the new min_headroom_mb is applied before or after CUDA graph reservation? We’ve been bitten by “double counting” in the past.

Samir Qureshi (author): Good call. It’s applied after graph/workspace reservation; I added an explicit comment + a startup log line emitting computed kv_cache_budget_bytes and headroom_bytes (see profile_startup_log.cc).
Irene Choi (review): +1 to raising headroom, but 2.5GB seems high for some of our smaller L40S instance types. Any risk we’re leaving too much GPU idle?

Samir Qureshi (author): On the smallest L40S nodes we still see enough budget for the target model set; the failure mode we’re addressing is allocator fragmentation under bursts. I added a guard in kv_cache_budget.cc: if computed KV budget would fall below a minimum functional threshold, we emit WARN and clamp compaction aggressiveness rather than silently starving KV cache.
Sofia Ivanova (review): Does earlier compaction affect scheduler fairness? We saw compaction spikes look like “compute stalls” in traces.

Samir Qureshi (author): Compaction is still bounded by the existing per-interval time budget; we’re only lowering the trigger utilization on L40S. Also added a counter in the regression test to ensure compaction time stays under the configured ceiling in the burst scenario.
Sahana Iyer (review): Tests look good but golden snapshots changed — can we ensure the schema version didn’t bump unexpectedly?
Samir Qureshi (author): Schema version unchanged; only L40S defaults changed. Added an assertion in profile_pack_golden_test.cc that schema_version stays constant for this PR.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved. The extra startup logging for computed budgets will help on-call a lot.
Irene Choi (approval): Approved with note: please ping Infra if you see throughput complaints so we can decide on an opt-in high-throughput profile later.
Sahana Iyer (approval): Approved. CI is green.
